external_entities.name: Reader
external_entities.description: A visitor to the public content site; some readers are signed in, others are anonymous. Readers fetch pages from the web server and static assets from the CDN.
external_entities.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in
external_entities.notes: The source does not distinguish signed-in and anonymous readers as separate actors, so they are modelled as one element.

external_entities.name: Admin
external_entities.description: An administrator who maintains the MySQL database directly rather than through the CMS, connecting from arbitrary locations with no jump host.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS
external_entities.notes: The source says nothing about how the admin authenticates or what credential they hold, so no asset tag is carried here; the direct-administration flow is what grounds claims about this path.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: Content delivery network that serves images, stylesheets and downloads to readers and hosts the bucket the web server publishes assets into.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.
external_entities.notes: The source names no CDN provider and does not say whether it is operated by the same party as the hosted network.

processes.name: Web server
processes.description: Serves the public content site over HTTPS and runs the CMS. Reads and writes pages, accounts and comments in MySQL and pushes newly published assets to the CDN bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.
processes.notes: The source treats 'the web server' and 'the CMS' as one deployed thing; modelled as a single process.

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: Holds pages, accounts and comments for the CMS. Sits on the same hosted network as the web server and is also reachable directly by the admin.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network
data_stores.notes: Not tagged credentials: the source says the database holds accounts, and what an account record contains is never stated. Sign-in exists for some readers, but where its secrets live is not described.

data_stores.name: CDN bucket
data_stores.description: Bucket behind the CDN holding images, stylesheets and downloads published from the web server.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket

data_flows.name: Page requests
data_flows.description: Readers request site pages from the web server over HTTPS; some readers are signed in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in
data_flows.authentication: sign-in exists for some readers; the mechanism, its strength and how sessions are handled are not stated
data_flows.data_description: Page requests and rendered site content

data_flows.name: Asset fetch
data_flows.description: Readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN over HTTP.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.
data_flows.encryption_in_transit: none — readers fetch these over HTTP

data_flows.name: CMS data
data_flows.description: The web server stores and retrieves pages, accounts and comments in the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network

data_flows.name: Asset publish
data_flows.description: When new assets are published the web server pushes them to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source states outright that how this push is authenticated is not described, which is why the attribute is unknown rather than absent.
data_flows.data_description: Newly published images, stylesheets and downloads

data_flows.name: Direct administration
data_flows.description: The admin connects straight to the database box over an unsecured MySQL connection with no TLS, from arbitrary locations and with no jump host, bypassing the CMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: That is an unsecured MySQL connection straight to the box, no TLS on it, and they do it from wherever they happen to be — there is no jump host.
data_flows.data_description: Direct database maintenance against pages, accounts and comments, performed outside the CMS
data_flows.encryption_in_transit: none — an unsecured MySQL connection, no TLS on it

trust_boundaries.name: Public internet
trust_boundaries.description: Everything outside the hosted network: readers on the public site and the admin connecting from wherever they happen to be.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS

trust_boundaries.name: Hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network carrying the web server running the CMS and the MySQL database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a MySQL database on the same hosted network

trust_boundaries.name: CDN
trust_boundaries.description: The content delivery network and its bucket, which serve static assets and are separate from the web server.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Images, stylesheets and downloads do not come off the web server.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: Described as the 'Public site' that 'readers hit ... over HTTPS'.

assumptions.assumption: The admin connects from outside the hosted network.
assumptions.basis: "they do it from wherever they happen to be — there is no jump host".

assumptions.assumption: The CDN and its bucket sit in a separate trust zone from the hosted network.
assumptions.basis: Assets 'do not come off the web server'; the web server 'pushes them up to the CDN's bucket', implying a distinct, separately operated location.
